name: webgpu-page-transition
title: WebGPU Page Transition
description: Image planes that morph between three views on one WebGPU canvas: a looping carousel, a draggable 3D float and a detail stack, with masked text reveals; WebGL 2 or plain images as fallbacks.
author: Ben Paine <https://github.com/bnpne>
docs:
Installed `WebGPUPageTransition` in `components/ui/` (five files, all prefixed `webgpu-page-transition`), with the `render-loop` helper in `lib/` and `use-reduced-motion` in `hooks/`. Render it in a sized box: `<WebGPUPageTransition className="h-svh" images={images} />`, where each image has `src`, `width`, `height` and optionally `caption` and `fact`.

It draws with three.js's WebGPU renderer, falls back to WebGL 2, and to plain images without either or under reduced motion. Control the view with `view` and `onViewChange` (`{ page: "main" }`, `{ page: "index" }`, `{ page: "inner", image: 2 }`). Needs `three`, `motion` and `lenis` (installed) and, for TypeScript, `@types/three`.

Ported from bnpne/page-transitions-with-webgpu-vanilla-js (MIT, copyright 2009 - 2025 Codrops), with its GSAP tweens and SplitText reveals rewritten in Motion; the license text is in each file.
